content.text:
I reviewed the three failures — all three are drawing-geometry/OCR defects, so the repair belongs in the authoritative figure briefs (FIG-4, FIG-5, FIG-7). No claim, description, numeral-table, or drawing-description text needed to move: the numerals shown on each sheet are unchanged, and every feature described still matches the disclosure.

**FIG. 4** — the renderer put the unnumbered downward passage inside shell side wall 14. The brief never said which way is outboard and never said the wall is solid, so I fixed the orientation and made the wall explicitly unbroken, with the passage confined inside the outline of frame 42.

**FIG. 5** — frame 42 was drawn as two disconnected hatched pieces (a natural reading of "frame body" plus "an upright passage inboard of the outboard web": a duct cut in section splits a frame into two limbs unless the section plane also cuts a web joining them). I made the frame one downwardly open channel profile — top web plus two depending limbs, continuously hatched — so duct 48 is the blank space between the limbs, opening 50 is the blank gap below their lower ends over passage 30, and nothing hatched can land in the lower left. Three hatched solids, as the brief requires.

**FIG. 7** — OCR read stray glyphs. I tightened the no-lettering rule to an exhaustive whitelist (caption plus the six numerals) and re-specified the three schematic elements most likely to render as letter-like forms: the spring, the latch, and the enclosure outline of indicator 80.

On prior art: the brief records that no search was run, so the art in `prior_art/` may be incomplete; nothing in this repair depends on it.
